The mainstream [LOCATION] foreign policy establishment views former President [PERSON] as a dangerous neo-isolationist, completely out of step with American ideals and interests. Internationalists at home and abroad shudder at the prospect of [ORGANIZATION]’s potential reelection in [DATE], fearing that he would dismantle the liberal order that [LOCATION] and its allies have built and defended since World War II. Such fears are justified; [ORGANIZATION] may indeed seek to do away with at least some core elements of the U.S.-led liberal order. But to portray his “[LOCATION] first” approach as a dark deviation from the American experience is to misunderstand its deep historical and ideological roots, as well as its considerable political appeal. [ORGANIZATION]’s statecraft is a response to a changing world and to demand signals from the [LOCATION] electorate, not a capricious effort to take apart the world that [LOCATION] made. None of this is to deny that [ORGANIZATION]’s return to office could be disastrous. At home, he may well imperil American democracy. Abroad, [ORGANIZATION]’s mere reelection would set the world on edge. [LOCATION] allies would have to face the reality that their security guarantor—the globe’s premier power—has been beset by intractable political dysfunction; they would have no choice but to question [ORGANIZATION]’s long-term reliability and make other plans. Meanwhile, autocrats would be emboldened and the cause of democracy everywhere debilitated. Yet the best [STREET] to avoid that highly unattractive outcome is not to recoil at [ORGANIZATION] first” movement or to see it merely as the work of a know-nothing felon. Rather, the [STREET] forward requires unpacking that movement, understanding its considerable political appeal, and appropriating its worthy elements. If the Democrats are to defeat [PERSON] and his neo-isolationist agenda, they should cull central elements of his “[LOCATION] first” program and pivot toward a more modest, restrained, and pragmatic brand of [LOCATION] statecraft. STEAL HIS THUNDER From [DATE] (with brief exceptions during the Spanish-American War and World War I), [LOCATION] embraced an isolationist grand strategy to which [ORGANIZATION]’s basic impulses bear a strong resemblance. In his Farewell Address of [DATE], President [PERSON] called for “as little political connection as possible” with foreign nations, declaring, “It is our true policy to steer clear of permanent alliances with any portion of the foreign world.” Isolationism endured well into [DATE], in no small part because its multiple ideological strains broadened its political appeal. Isolationism offered something for everyone, enabling it to long have a lock on [LOCATION] politics. For realists, isolationism properly reflected and reinforced geographic insulation and strategic detachment. For idealists and progressives, isolationism meant escaping realpolitik and enabling investment in the country’s economic well-being rather than in instruments of war. Conservative nationalists looked to isolationism to defend sovereignty and strengthen the unilateral exercise of [LOCATION] power. Libertarians saw the strategy as a means of securing small government and domestic freedom. For anti-immigrant groups, isolationism meant preserving social homogeneity by keeping the nonwhite world at bay. Industrialists saw isolationism as an extension of protectionism—keeping imports, rather than migrants, at bay. Fearful that the expansionist ambitions of Nazi [LOCATION] and imperial [LOCATION] would entangle [LOCATION] in great-power rivalry, the isolationist camp in [DATE] founded [ORGANIZATION], which did its best to keep the nation far away from World War II. But the Japanese attack on [LOCATION], in [DATE], shattered the isolationist consensus. [LOCATION]’ entry into World War II marked a historical inflection point, clearing the [STREET] for the nation’s embrace of an expansive internationalism. Soon thereafter, the onset of the Cold War accelerated the country’s appetite for global engagement. By [DATE], it was liberal internationalism, not isolationism, that had captured [LOCATION] politics. The projection of American power and the creation and defense of an open, multilateral order among like-minded democracies had come to pay dividends across the political spectrum. The result was a centrist and bipartisan compact behind liberal internationalism. That compact long served as the political foundation of Pax Americana. If the Democrats are to defeat [PERSON] and his neo-isolationist agenda, they should cull central elements of his “[LOCATION] first” program. [DATE], however, that internationalist consensus has shattered—just as the isolationist consensus did in [DATE]. [LOCATION]’s purposes abroad are no longer in equilibrium with its domestic means. Deindustrialization and the hollowing out of the middle class, [DATE] of strategic overreach and hyperglobalization, and the influx of immigrants and rapid shifts in the country’s demographic makeup are combining to bring back into political vogue the multiple ideological strains of isolationism that previously shaped [LOCATION] grand strategy. Enter [PERSON]. “The forgotten men and women of our country will be forgotten no longer,” he pledged in his inaugural address, in [DATE]. “From this moment on, it’s going to be [LOCATION] first. Every decision on trade, on taxes, on immigration, on foreign affairs, will be made to benefit American workers and American families.” Rather than resisting the public’s call for an inward turn, [PERSON] amplified it, promising to free the [LOCATION] government from its foreign burdens and focus its attention and resources on the home front. That promise won the support of many millions of Americans that felt—and still feel—left behind by liberal internationalism. Trump fell far short of his pledge to get working Americans back on their feet—an electoral liability but also one of the reasons that his politics of grievance and neo-isolationist impulses still have considerable public appeal. The country is now in the midst of a tug of war over its role in the world. If the Democrats want to defeat the new “America first” movement, they need to better understand it, and then steal [ORGANIZATION]’s thunder by borrowing its most appealing components. [ORGANIZATION], THEN AND NOW After the errant attempt of the original [LOCATION] First movement to keep [LOCATION] out of World War II , “isolationism” became a dirty word. Ever since, internationalists have deployed the term to tar and feather the likes of the conservative commentator [PERSON], the former Republican member of [ORGANIZATION] [PERSON], and now [PERSON], charging that they are naively deluded about the desirability and viability of strategic detachment. Internationalists contend that even if isolationism may have made sense in [DATE], when expansive oceans to the [LOCATION] and [LOCATION] afforded [LOCATION] natural security, [DATE]’s world provides no such luxury. Due to numerous developments—including ballistic missiles, economic interdependence, the connectedness of cyberspace, and climate change—strategic detachment and going it alone are no longer viable options. This critique of isolationism is valid; [LOCATION] can never again enjoy the natural security that it once did. But the original conception of isolationism rested on the advantages not just of geographic separation but also of non-entanglement. Were [PERSON] to fail to honor [ORGANIZATION]’s commitment to collective defense, he would have a solid precedent. In [DATE], [PERSON] unilaterally reneged on the alliance that [LOCATION] had concluded with [LOCATION] in [DATE] to secure French help during the Revolutionary War. The main reason for this act of “ignominious perfidy,” as the [LOCATION] representative [PERSON] called the move, was that [LOCATION] deemed it to be contrary to the national interest for the country to be dragged into another war with [LOCATION]. [LOCATION] did not conclude another military alliance for [DATE], when it did so through [ORGANIZATION] and [ORGANIZATION] after World War II. This preference for non-entanglement was also the principal source of opposition to the commitment to collective security contained in [ORGANIZATION] covenant. Senator [PERSON], an Idaho Republican and a leading opponent of ratifying the treaty that created the league, argued that [LOCATION] membership would mean that “we have forfeited and surrendered, once and for all, the great policy of ‘no entangling alliances’ upon which the strength of this [LOCATION] has been founded.” [PERSON]’s skepticism toward nation building and the promotion of democracy abroad resonates with the isolationist posture of early [LOCATION]. In similar fashion, [ORGANIZATION] brand of isolationism is motivated more by unilateralism than by a search for strategic detachment. “I am skeptical of international unions that tie us up and bring [LOCATION] down,” [PERSON] has declared, insisting that “we will never enter [LOCATION] into any agreement that reduces our ability to control our own affairs.” He has informed [ORGANIZATION] that “we will never surrender [LOCATION]’s sovereignty to an unelected, unaccountable global bureaucracy.” For [ORGANIZATION], alliances qualify as “unions that tie us up,” especially when allies do not shoulder their fair share of the defense burden. [ORGANIZATION]’s stiff-necked unilateralism is self-defeating, alienating the allies that [LOCATION] needs in order to defend common interests and secure collective action. But his cautionary stance toward entanglement does help inoculate [LOCATION] against chronic overreach. Trump initiated the process of ending [LOCATION]’s disastrous war in [LOCATION]. He has reportedly questioned the wisdom of granting [LOCATION] membership in [ORGANIZATION]—with good reason. [ORGANIZATION]’s declaration of an “irreversible” commitment to [LOCATION]’s membership, which would obligate [ORGANIZATION] to defend the country if attacked, is fundamentally at odds with the alliance’s current unwillingness to go to war in [LOCATION]’s defense. [PERSON], [ORGANIZATION]’s running mate, is wrong to oppose further [LOCATION] aid to [LOCATION], but he is right on some things. “The [PERSON] administration has no viable plan for the Ukrainians to win this war,” he correctly noted in an essay for [ORGANIZATION] in [DATE]. “The sooner Americans confront this truth, the sooner we can fix this mess and broker for peace.” The American public deserves a sober and realistic debate about the nature and salience of the [LOCATION] interests at stake in [LOCATION]. The American electorate also deserves to be told the truth: that [LOCATION] is highly unlikely to succeed in expelling Russian forces from its territory, even with the continuation of strong support from the [LOCATION]. [ORGANIZATION]’s readiness to seek a negotiated settlement is not capitulation: it is pragmatism. THE WORLD AS IT IS Trump’s skepticism toward nation building and the promotion of democracy abroad also resonates with the isolationist posture of early [LOCATION]. To be sure, Americans from the founding era onward believed that they were embarking on a unique experiment in building republican government, an experiment that they were ultimately destined to share with the rest of the world. Yet the founders and their successors were appropriately doubtful of [LOCATION]’ ability to engineer political change abroad and therefore understood that they needed to spread democracy primarily by example. As then Secretary of [ORGANIZATION] [PERSON] famously stated in [DATE], [LOCATION] “goes not abroad in search of monsters to destroy.” So, too, did successive [LOCATION] presidents appreciate the need to operate in the world as it is, working with democracies and nondemocracies alike in the pursuit of [LOCATION] interests. Even as President [PERSON] warned [LOCATION]’s great powers in [DATE] against any “future colonization” in [LOCATION], he acknowledged and accepted [LOCATION]’s political preferences. It was the policy of [LOCATION], he asserted, “not to interfere in the internal concerns of any of its powers; to consider the government de facto as the legitimate government for us; to cultivate friendly relations with it.” [PERSON] took this ideological variant of isolationism too far during his presidency, exhibiting a fondness for autocrats such as Russian President [PERSON] and North Korean leader [PERSON] while giving a cold shoulder to the leaders of allied democracies. But [ORGANIZATION]’s approach to grand strategy does exhibit due caution to the promotion of democracy abroad. He correctly traced [LOCATION]’ overreach in [LOCATION] to the “dangerous idea that we could make Western democracies out of countries that had no experience or interests in becoming a Western democracy.” He told [ORGANIZATION] that “we do not seek to impose our [STREET] of life on anyone” and that “I honor the right of every nation in this room to pursue its own customs, beliefs, and traditions.” In an interdependent and globalized world, [ORGANIZATION]’s pragmatic readiness to work across ideological dividing lines may produce better results than positing [DATE] as “a battle between democracy and autocracy,” as President [PERSON] has done. [LOCATION]’ early embrace of isolationism also emerged from the firm belief of the founders that ambition abroad would come at the expense of freedom and prosperity at home. Entanglement in great-power rivalries would require a large federal government and military establishment, which would in turn threaten tyranny at home and divert resources that would be better spent on productive domestic investment. When it comes to the defense of liberty at home, [ORGANIZATION] unquestionably breaks with American traditions, having attempted to overturn the outcome of the [DATE] election and expressed interest in imposing exactly the kind of tyranny that the founders feared. Yet [PERSON]’s attacks against what he deems the “deep state” resonate with libertarian skepticism of the federal government. And even though he supports the sizable military establishment that the founders opposed, [ORGANIZATION] has effectively portrayed nation building and foreign aid as a wasteful distraction, arguing that [LOCATION] should be spending taxpayer money solving problems at home rather than abroad. Many Americans agree. BORDERS AND BARRIERS On immigration, [ORGANIZATION]’s program is in line with the anti-immigrant sentiment that accompanied the nation’s long embrace of isolationism. In [DATE], [LOCATION] expansion into the [LOCATION] and [LOCATION] was blocked by widespread public and elite opposition to bringing more [LOCATION], Hispanic, and Catholic people into the [LOCATION] body politic. [LOCATION] did annex over half of [LOCATION] at the end of the Mexican-American War (1846–48), but the [LOCATION] government wanted not [LOCATION]’s people but its land, which was soon settled by whites. The intensification of isolationism during the interwar era coincided with a surge in anti-immigrant fervor. In [DATE], [ORGANIZATION] passed legislation that reduced the number of Jews and Catholics coming into the country by 90 percent and barred immigration from [LOCATION] entirely. During [DATE], [LOCATION] deported about a million immigrants from [LOCATION], many of whom were [LOCATION] citizens. [ORGANIZATION]’s brand of neo-isolationism is tinged by a similar embrace of anti-immigrant sentiment. As president, he cut back on immigrant quotas, made insulting references to minorities, and strove to build a wall on the border with [LOCATION]. [PERSON] is now campaigning on an anti-immigrant platform, pledging to deport millions of undocumented migrants, who, he insists, are “poisoning the blood of our country.” Many Americans see immigration as the top challenge facing the country, which is why most Democrats also see an urgent need to fix the system. [PERSON] worked hard to secure a bipartisan overhaul of immigration policy, but Republicans, at [ORGANIZATION]’s prompting, sank that effort [DATE]. Thereafter, [PERSON] took the extraordinary step of issuing an executive order providing for temporary closure of the southern border when the [DATE] average of [DATE] illegal crossings exceeds 2,500. [ORGANIZATION] has also resuscitated the protectionism that long guided the nation’s economic statecraft. Even though [LOCATION] from its earliest days relied heavily on commerce with other nations, it sought fair rather than free trade and relied on tariffs for revenue and to protect domestic industries. [LOCATION]’ geopolitical retreat of the [DATE] coincided with a sharp pullback on the trade front; the [ORGANIZATION] of [DATE] triggered the fragmentation of the global economy and the collapse of international trade. During his presidency, [ORGANIZATION] relied heavily on the protectionist component of the isolationist playbook. He renegotiated [ORGANIZATION], ended efforts to conclude the Trans-Pacific Partnership and [ORGANIZATION], and announced a wide range of tariffs. [ORGANIZATION] has pledged to impose a raft of new tariffs if reelected, including 60 percent on all Chinese goods and ten percent on products from the rest of the world. [ORGANIZATION] has even floated the idea of turning back time to [DATE] by eliminating the personal income tax and relying on tariffs for all federal revenue. (A federal income tax was introduced temporarily during the Civil War but not regularized until [DATE].) Once again, [PERSON] is responding to demand signals from the electorate, seeking to appeal to the many Americans who have suffered economic dislocation as a result of automation and free trade. It is no surprise that [PERSON] has not only continued to rely on tariffs (particularly on Chinese goods) to promote manufacturing and has also turned to industrial policy to create jobs, advance economic security, and fight climate change. PREEMPTING “AMERICA FIRST” [ORGANIZATION] brand of [LOCATION] statecraft has deep roots in the American experience and, like the original version of isolationism, has something for almost everyone, giving it broad appeal across the American electorate. Democrats dismiss his “[LOCATION] first” agenda as strategic delusion at their own peril. Instead, they should preempt it by embracing its best elements. Democrats need to find the middle ground between an expansive liberal internationalism that is no longer sustainable at home or abroad and the dangerous isolationist excesses that would likely accompany [PERSON] return to the presidency. That middle ground entails standing by [PERSON]’s multilateralism and his investment in old alliances and new partnerships, moves that have resuscitated U.S.-led collective action and restored the nation’s image as a team player. At the same time, [LOCATION] must avoid the bouts of strategic overreach, such as in [LOCATION] and [LOCATION], that encourage the electorate to gravitate toward isolationist alternatives. The investigation and trial will play out below the fold for a while; maybe it will return to the spotlight in time for the verdict and sentencing. But it has been over [DATE], and that is about as long of a life cycle as a story like this can expect with the brutal churn of [DATE] news cycle and the relentless march of new tragedies. These stories are, sadly, too common now to hold our attention for long. “Mass” ([DATE]), written and directed by [PERSON], is concerned with the questions we ask in the wake of a school shooting. For the characters, those questions are deeply personal. In “Mass” the shooter is [PERSON], the son of [PERSON] ([PERSON]) and [PERSON] (Reed Birney); [PERSON], the son of [PERSON] ([PERSON]) and [PERSON] ([PERSON]), was one of the victims. [DATE], the four parents meet in the basement of an [ORGANIZATION] church to talk and try to heal. [PERSON] and [PERSON] say that their therapist encouraged them to be curious instead of interrogating. But as the conversation goes on, they are drawn again and again to the agonizing mystery at the heart of [ORGANIZATION] act: Why did this happen? And how can we prevent it from happening again? By focusing on parental grief, “Mass” grounds us in human tragedy even as it touches on the political and social implications of [ORGANIZATION] act. In one heartbreaking exchange, the fathers admit that they recognized the tape outlines of their children’s bodies when police let them walk through the school. While it would be easy to reserve our empathy for [PERSON] and [PERSON], the film challenges us to feel for both sets of parents. [PERSON] and [PERSON] are wracked with guilt as they reflect on how they might have failed their son. But we also see their love for him and their agony at not being able to grieve his loss publicly because of what he did before he died. The film invites us to sit with the questions and eludes easy answers. The parents discuss possibilities: Was the catalyst the fact that [PERSON] was changing schools, was part of an online gaming community or was going to the gun range with friends? Did [PERSON]’s parents see the signs and fail to act? Or was [PERSON] broken from the start, destined for a violent end? Some of these elements are suggestive (it is notable that even when the characters disagree, no one denies that access to guns is a problem), but they never form a cohesive picture, a definitive solution. The unspoken question, evoked by the film’s religious setting, is: Where is God in all of this? It is the most existential of all, but also—paradoxically—the one that the film comes closest to answering. The name of the church is [PERSON], and at one point a character stands framed beside a banner with the literal translation: “GOD WITH [LOCATION].” Where is God in the midst of horror and tragedy? God is with us. God is in the room with these four people as they try to understand and to heal. God is there when one character makes the difficult choice to offer forgiveness, and God is there when another—carrying a heavy burden of rage and grief—is struck by the delicate beauty of a choir’s song. Between the time I began writing this column and finishing it, there was already another school shooting, in [LOCATION]. A [DATE] boy was seriously hurt and a [DATE] boy is now in custody. No one was killed this time, a grim silver lining. “Mass” doesn’t offer us solutions; like the characters, we need to find those solutions on our own and work to make them real. But the film reminds us that we are not alone, even in the face of great loss and endless questions. And when we come together to heal, make peace and imagine a better world for our children, God is with us. “Mass” is streaming on Hulu. The draft prepared beforehand called abortion “a preeminent priority” for the bishops, but not — in a rhetorical switch — their most important issue in political life. Editors at The [ORGANIZATION] website obtained a copy of the proposed language and published a news story. “Well, a number of bishops read that in The [ORGANIZATION],” noted [PERSON], one of the website’s two founders, “so several of them proposed amendments to change the text to stronger language. ... More than one bishop told us he was only informed about the issue because he read it in The [ORGANIZATION].” The final text included this phrase: “The threat of abortion remains our preeminent priority.” In moral theology terms, “a preeminent priority” is quite different from a statement that abortion remains “our preeminent priority.” That bright red line has caused fierce debates, especially with a pro-abortion-rights Catholic in [LOCATION]. A heated opinion piece would have generated as many, or more, reader clicks than a hard news report, which would have been “good for business,” noted Condon. Opinion is cheap. Reporting is expensive. “We don’t have ads on our site, which means we don’t make a penny from page views,” he wrote in the website’s newsletter. That was a strategic choice, “because we don’t ever want to set ourselves up with a perverse incentive to write sensationalist stories we aren’t sure about.” In the heated environs of Catholic cyberspace, that kind of reporting will draw fierce criticism from partisans on the other side of doctrinal debates that have political, moral and cultural implications. Catholic liberals and many mainstream journalists screamed “foul” when The [ORGANIZATION] published several [DATE] stories — built on patterns in cellphone data — claiming that some important Catholic clergy in [LOCATION] and in non-tourist zones inside the [LOCATION] were using the [PERSON] app [PERSON]. A [ORGANIZATION] column called this coverage “unethical, homophobic innuendo.” Then again, The [ORGANIZATION]’s editors fielded scathing emails and texts after a recent report claiming that [ORGANIZATION] had been investigated in [DATE] after accusations of minimal financial oversight and glaring irregularities — including one official attempting to remove “shopping bags full of cash.” The key: This powerful doctrinal department was, at that time, led by German Cardinal [PERSON], a hero among conservative Catholics. The cardinal blamed the incidents on accounting errors, while also accusing The [ORGANIZATION] of violating the Eighth Commandment: “You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.” At the moment, The [ORGANIZATION] is taking heat from conservatives for coverage raising questions about remarks by Sen. [PERSON] — a prominent Catholic convert and the [ORGANIZATION] candidate for vice president — defending legal access to mifepristone, an abortifacient pharmaceutical commonly called the “abortion pill.” The [ORGANIZATION] has requested a [ORGANIZATION] interview to clarify his stance, asking whether — should he remain the Republican spokesman on this issue — his words and actions might fit the “obstinately persist” standard that would cause trouble under Catholic canon law. “The bishops of this country ... have been arguing about whether Catholic politicians supportive of legal protection for abortion should be admitted to [ORGANIZATION],” wrote coeditor [PERSON] in a newsletter commentary. The question some Catholics will ask is “whether what’s good for the goose is good for the gander — and whether the bishops who discussed prohibiting Democrat pols from the [ORGANIZATION] will take the discussion across party lines.” [PERSON] and [PERSON] are both canon lawyers as well as journalists. As co-owners of The [ORGANIZATION], they want to continue to stress [DATE] news reports, as well as deeper investigations into the legal, financial and doctrinal details of Catholic life. Also, instead of pushing for reforms that modernize church doctrines and traditions, the website seeks reforms in which the behaviors of church leaders “match the doctrines the church is trying to teach and defend,” said [PERSON], reached by telephone. “For us, reform goes part and parcel with promoting true renewal — a greater flourishing of the church’s mission. The presidential debate reminded me why. Will the young women of [DATE] feel freer to pursue their vocations without worrying about fitting into narrow gender roles? [ORGANIZATION] Justice [PERSON] Published [DATE], I had no television, so we rarely had a chance to watch political debates. But [DATE], watching these events is a family affair. We’ve seen debates that were comical, disturbing, depressing, occasionally impressive. But even when a debate seems more like bad stand-up comedy than serious politics, I try to provide my kids with enough information to understand the basic issues. I hope they will stay politically educated and civically engaged and be well equipped to assess data and make political decisions regardless of social pressure. [TIME]’s presidential debate provided us with multiple opportunities for a giggle. As [LOCATION] residents we laughed at the memes about our pets being eaten (our pets are fine) but also discussed the racism latent in [PERSON] talk about immigrants devouring cats and dogs. But despite the dystopian atmosphere pervading our national politics, watching the debate left me energized. It is exciting to know that, even in a world filled with violence and injustice, my daughter can witness women being courageous, forceful, and empathetic not only in a domestic sphere but on a national stage. It’s not that I didn’t have women to look up to as a child. My mother modeled creativity and community building; my grandmother modeled resilience and independence. As a teenager, I looked up to the women who taught me how to ride and handle horses. But then I entered a very conservative college. When I chose, in that space, to pursue an academic career, I had a sense of entering an unexplored country. Advertisement That sense was based on residing in an anachronism, a cultural bubble where people were deliberate about their rejection not only of current social progress, but of past progress as well. In the philosophy department at my college, there were no women teachers. In my entire time as a student, not just as an undergraduate but in both my graduate programs, I had only four women professors. And in my undergraduate program, at an institution where people seriously debated questions like “Is it moral for women to have jobs at all?” or “Should women be allowed to wear pants?” simply identifying as a feminist could get one attacked and excluded. At a different school, I would have encountered more women in academia, even celebrated scholars. Yes, this would have meant navigating questions of identity, liberation, and intersectionality, like, “What are the limits to our obligations to support other women?” or even “Is wearing makeup something we do for ourselves, or for the patriarchy?” But these would have been questions relating to our bodily existence in the world, not to an abstract “essence of femininity” we felt compelled to instantiate. Even as I grew more adept at doing the work of philosophy, I felt like an outsider, not because of ability, but because I had no sense of how to perform the role I had chosen. The young men in my philosophy program could look at our all-male faculty and get a sense of who they wanted to be. I could not do this in quite the same [STREET]. Even superficial things like how to dress professionally, or figuring out the limits of appropriate humor, were all male coded. Advertisement I said that I was living in an anachronism. But many communities across our nation, and many churches and schools, tacitly held the same assumptions about women that dictated my life: We were too emotional to be good leaders. Our real vocation was in the home. We ought to focus more on how to please men. Pursuing a career was selfish. I remember how media personalities, and not just conservative ones, mocked women in politics in [DATE]. Dress codes alone sent a message that we were second-[STREET] to men in the workplace or in the political sphere. Men had a uniform, the suit and tie. Women did not. When a woman dressed professionally, she had to steer between seeming too feminine, and therefore frail, and too masculine, and therefore unnatural. This prejudice was clearly still around in [DATE], with the jokes about women in pantsuits. None of this has stopped women from claiming our places at the table. But even in [DATE], we still get pushback specifically because of our gender. Every time a movie features a complex and authoritative woman as a hero, people get angry. Multiple movements exist, including one of our two major political parties, that want to put women back into the small domestic boxes where we used to be trapped. And women who are queer, non-white, or disabled face additional pressure to be smaller, less-than, quieter, even nonexistent. As [PERSON] parent raising a Gen-Z daughter, I want to tell her that the world is filled with exciting opportunities for adventure, creativity, and activism. But I must warn her, too, that the world is filled with dangers. It is also filled with people, including other women, who will tell her, even in [DATE], that she must conform to narrow gender roles if she wants to be respected or successful. Advertisement While our culture has made enormous advances in gender justice, people in progressive areas may not be aware that those advances are not always visible in some pockets of the nation. There are still areas where people use scripture to control women, or where any woman who steps over the guardrails around “traditional femininity” is mocked and ostracized. And some of the people calling the shots in those spaces would like to call the shots for the whole [LOCATION]. So, yes, it was exciting to sit beside my daughter and watch Vice President [PERSON] debating former President [PERSON] on the national stage, to see her model authenticity, assertiveness, humor, empathy, and boundary-setting. I hope that the young women of [DATE] will feel freer to seek their paths in life without pausing to worry about things like gender roles or “the feminine genius” or “what men want.” I have become critical of the concept of role models, because humans are individuals. And I think it is always dangerous to view anyone as a hero or infallible authority. As a teenager without a role model, I shouldn’t have worried so much about uncharted territory, especially since it really wasn’t uncharted. But this, too, is a gender expectation placed on women. We’re admonished for stepping over the cute little white picket fences that have been installed to keep us in our [STREET]. Still, having mentors and examples with shared life experiences can be important for personal formation, especially during the turbulent teens and 20s. And seeing women who have claimed their right to be fully human can inspire us to do the same. Advertisement It is unfortunate that in so many Christian churches, women are still treated as second-class citizens. I don’t want the message my daughter takes from our faith to be that she is less capable than men of leading, inspiring, and making decisions. I don’t want her to believe she is less capable of imaging Christ . And I know that as I encourage her to live out her creative vocation, whatever that may be, we are both going to encounter multiple challenges from a world that will tell us both we are transgressing our boundaries. But I am glad that she has so many more opportunities than I had to see women stepping lightly over those boundaries into the larger world. Attorneys general call for surgeon general’s warning A bipartisan group of 42 state attorneys general recently called for the [LOCATION] surgeon general to add a health warning to algorithm-driven social media sites. Credit: SynthEx/Shutterstock By Jonah McKeown Follow + [DATE] at [TIME] ET · Updated [DATE] at [TIME] A bipartisan group of 42 state attorneys general recently called for the [LOCATION] surgeon general to add a health warning to algorithm-driven social media sites, citing the potential psychological harm that such sites can have on children and teenagers. “As state attorneys general, we sometimes disagree about important issues, but all of us share an abiding concern for the safety of the kids in our jurisdictions — and algorithm-driven social media platforms threaten that safety,” the coalition of attorneys general wrote in a [DATE] letter to congressional leaders. The attorneys general cited growing bodies of research that link young people’s use of these platforms to psychological harm, including depression, anxiety, and even suicidal thoughts in kids and teens. They also noted how platforms feature “enticing algorithmic recommendations, infinite scrolling, and a constant stream of notifications, which are designed to keep kids relentlessly engaged on the platforms, even at the expense of taking breaks, engaging in other activities, or sleeping.” State attorneys general have taken action in [DATE] to hold the largest social media platforms accountable. In [DATE], the attorneys general of 45 states and [LOCATION] filed a series of lawsuits against [ORGANIZATION], the parent company of [ORGANIZATION], alleging that the company “deployed harmful and manipulative product features designed to push young users’ engagement with the [ORGANIZATION] platform to dangerous levels, all while representing to the public that its products are safe.” In addition, some states, including [LOCATION], [LOCATION], [LOCATION], [LOCATION], [LOCATION], [LOCATION], and [LOCATION], have commenced litigation against [ORGANIZATION] for violating their state’s consumer protection laws, they noted. “[A] surgeon general’s warning on social media platforms, though not sufficient to address the full scope of the problem, would be one consequential step toward mitigating the risk of harm to youth. A warning would not only highlight the inherent risks that social media platforms presently pose for young people but also complement other efforts to spur attention, research, and investment into the oversight of social media platforms,” the attorneys general wrote. “This problem will not solve itself and the social media platforms have demonstrated an unwillingness to fix the problem on their own. Therefore, we urge [ORGANIZATION] to act by requiring warnings on algorithm-driven social media platforms, as recommended by the surgeon general.” [ORGANIZATION] General [PERSON] has on several occasions signaled a willingness to highlight the health risks posed by social media, issuing in 2023 a 25-page advisory regarding social media usage evidence for its negative effects. “Children are exposed to harmful content on social media, ranging from violent and sexual content to bullying and harassment. And for too many children, social media use is compromising their sleep and valuable in-person time with family and friends,” [PERSON] wrote in that advisory. “We are in the middle of a national youth mental health crisis, and I am concerned that social media is an important driver of that crisis — one that we must urgently address.” In [DATE], [ORGANIZATION] voted overwhelmingly to advance extensive regulations that its supporters say will protect the safety and privacy of children on the internet. Under the bill, the government would impose a “duty of care” on social media platforms, meaning social media companies could be held legally liable if they are negligent in their efforts to prevent children from accessing harmful material. Bullying and harassment, as well as sexual and violent material, are listed as harmful material covered by the legislation, known as the Kids Online Safety Act (KOSA) and [ORGANIZATION] (COPPA 2.0). The legislation would also require platforms to work to prevent children from accessing material that could contribute to anxiety, depression, eating disorders, and various other harm. Fresh off a difficult visit to [LOCATION] , where the church’s clergy sex abuse scandal and its treatment of women troubled the pope at every turn, [PERSON] led top cardinals in apologizing for everything from the destruction of the planet to the discrimination of women and rejection of migrants. “How can we be credible in our mission if we don’t recognize our own errors and bow down to heal the wounds that we have caused with our sins?” [PERSON] asked. ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW The penitential service in [LOCATION] preceded the official start [DATE] of the synod, a [DATE] meeting of more than 360 bishops and lay people to discuss the future of the church. The most pressing agenda items include calls for women to have greater decision-making roles in the church. The [LOCATION] organized the vigil service as a [STREET] to prepare spiritually for the meeting, on the grounds that naming sins and asking for their forgiveness was a necessary step to begin again. In one dramatic moment during the service, a man who was sexually violated by a priest as a child, [PERSON], told his story to a hushed basilica. He denounced the “veil of secrecy,” and lack of transparency and accountability in the church’s response to abuse, which he said had shaken the faith of millions. “When an institution as prominent as [ORGANIZATION] fails to protect its most vulnerable members, it sends a message that justice and accountability are negotiable — when in reality, they should be fundamental,” he said. Cardinal [PERSON], [PERSON]’ longtime adviser on child protection strategies, was called on to read out the request for forgiveness for the abuse scandal, one of seven top cardinals who read aloud petitions for forgiveness that [PERSON] himself had written. “I ask forgiveness, feeling shame, for all the times we have used the condition of ordained ministry and consecrated life to commit this terrible sin, feeling safe and protected while we were profiting diabolically from the little ones and the poor,” said [ORGANIZATION], the retired archbishop of [LOCATION]. The abuse and cover-up scandal that has convulsed the church for [DATE] has devastated the credibility of the Catholic hierarchy in many countries and helped contribute to sharp declines in the faith. Internally, the crisis has fueled calls for broader reform to de-emphasize the importance of priests and value more the contributions of rank-and-file Catholics, especially women. Not one to give up, [PERSON] responded to an advertisement in [ORGANIZATION] and purchased 100 rosary pieces to see if that was an item he could make as well as sell. Although he, himself, was Jewish, he had learned from several Roman Catholic friends the importance of rosary beads for counting prayers. With his experience crafting jewelry items using beads and ornaments, he had found a niche in creating rosaries and selling them. As a supplier, his company would enable others including church related organizations to have their own business. Joining [PERSON] to work in the new facility were his [DATE] son [PERSON], his [DATE] daughter [PERSON], and her husband, [PERSON]. Having a machinist background and a sense of inventiveness, [PERSON] enjoyed tinkering and made a lot of the furnishings and devices in his home. When he owned the tire business, he had invented and patented a special retreading machine. In the new Pittshire facility he designed labor-saving equipment like a wire measuring and cutting machine for the production of rosaries. [PERSON]Reuters Vatican meeting ends and hope fades for more change under [PERSON] By [PERSON], [PERSON] The Washington Post [DATE] [DATE] Updated Oct 27, [DATE] Facebook Twitter Linkedin SMS [PERSON] Twitter Linkedin SMS Email Print Save Facebook Twitter Linkedin SMS Email Print Save VATICAN CITY - The [LOCATION]’s most highly anticipated gathering since [DATE] [DATE] with the thorniest issues facing the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics largely unanswered. The Synod of Bishops, which met in [DATE] and again [DATE] pledged administrative changes that could give more power to local dioceses. But it referred questions on the ordination of female deacons, further outreach to the LGBTQ+ community and married priests for further study. The outcome calmed the fears of church conservatives that Pope [PERSON] “Synod on Synodality” would serve as a smokescreen for radical change while leaving liberals, who had seen it as their best opportunity since Vatican II to promote reform, empty-handed for now. “It’s hard to say whether this synod has actually taken any decision,” said [PERSON], a Catholic theologian at [ORGANIZATION]. The document that it produced amounts to a set of guidelines on a range of challenges. On the abuse crisis, for example, the synod concluded that “it is necessary to [offer] training for those working with minors and vulnerable adults.” On hostility toward migrants: “All … are called to build intercultural communities.” On transparency and accountability in the church, “it is necessary to have structures and methods for regularly evaluating the exercise of ministry.” Other issues were taken off the table and sent to study groups before the second and final session of the [DATE] event opened [DATE]. The 10 groups are supposed to report back with their findings in [DATE]. It remains unclear whether and how [PERSON] will respond. The most unconventional pope in modern history has in [DATE] taken polemic steps - most notably backing brief blessings by priests of same-sex couples. There are proposals he has publicly opposed and on which he appears unlikely to change his mind, including the ordination of women deacons or married priests. But unlike his predecessors, [PERSON], [DATE], has not shut those conversations down. “He is the pope of surprises,” said the Rev. [PERSON], an American priest who has written several books about the inner workings of [ORGANIZATION]. “I don’t think he’s done, but I don’t know what he’s going do. I don’t think that anyone does.” In an unusual move, [PERSON] wrapped up the synod by announcing that he wouldn’t follow up its final document with an apostolic exhortation: “What we have approved is enough.” [PERSON], president of the conservative [ORGANIZATION], said the synod had “managed to make everyone unhappy.” “That’s perhaps especially true for liberals, some of whom were expecting a Vatican III,” he said. “Well, this wasn’t it.” Vatican II was the council convened in [DATE] to modernize the church for an increasingly secular world. It ordered epochal revisions - changing the language of the Mass, turning the priest around to face the people and promoting interfaith dialogue, among others. Before [PERSON]’s synod, the [LOCATION] worked to temper expectations, calling it a listening exercise more than anything else and a chance for the global church to dialogue. Its makeup was historic: The church’s leading consultative body was previously reserved for senior clerics; now, for the first time, lay people, including women, were given votes. In announcing the synod in [DATE], [PERSON] asked regional churches to name topics they wanted discussed. They included the elevation of the role of women and whether and how to minister to divorced Catholics, the LBGTQ+ community and polygamists. Regional churches asked for more concrete steps to prevent clerical sexual abuse and offer justice to victims. But from the beginning, victims’ rights groups denounced the synod, saying it wasn’t taking the issue seriously enough. An initial session [DATE] revealed deep divisions, particularly over LGBTQ+ Catholics and female deacons. With those issues off the agenda before [DATE]’s session, the atmosphere, delegates said, appeared more amicable. “Of course, because everything important was taken off the table,” one delegate said, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss the closed-door synod. In a final document released [DATE], the synod wrote that “the question of women’s access to diaconal ministry remains open. This discernment needs to continue.” The body also called for “giving more space to the contributions of female saints, theologians and mystics.” The role of women in the church, specifically the question of ordaining women as deacons, became one of the gathering’s most divisive topics. On [DATE], during what synod delegates thought would be an informational meeting on the study group on the role of women, the [LOCATION] put forward two nonmember “ambassadors” who were unable to answer most questions. Some delegates were angered by what they saw as a dismissal of the topic. To address their frustration, Cardinal [PERSON], the head of [ORGANIZATION], met with those delegates [DATE]. [PERSON] is on the record opposing the ordination of women as deacons. On [DATE], however, [ORGANIZATION] said the pope was open to more study on the issue and a preexisting church commission would continue to examine the topic. But the new study group, he said, would only look at how to expand women’s “power” within the church as part of the laity. He said women want to be heard and valued, but most were not asking to be ordained. One study, published in [DATE] , alleged that “[LOCATION] states with the most restrictive abortion laws saw 16% more infant deaths” from 2014–2018, before Roe’s repeal. Another study published [DATE] reached similar conclusions for infant mortality rates post-repeal, finding that “infant mortality was higher than expected, overall and among those with congenital anomalies, for [DATE] after the [ORGANIZATION] decision.” Those findings have led to significant media coverage, with pro-abortion supporters citing the data as evidence that abortion bans are harmful not just allegedly to women but to children as well. ‘Now we’re paying attention to them’ Skop told [ORGANIZATION] that it’s wrong to link pro-life laws to higher infant mortality rates. “There are a lot of pro-abortion media articles that are trying to imply a connection between infant deaths and pro-life laws,” she said, “when what we’re seeing may be natural variations in mortality.” Historically, approximately 20% of infant deaths are related to congenital anomalies, [ORGANIZATION] said. “Obviously, it’s intuitive that pro-life laws are not causing an increase in those abnormalities occurring in the first [STREET],” she said. In many cases, children with genetic abnormalities are now being brought to birth and then dying from those abnormalities after birth, she said. “Because we do not care to keep mandatory statistics on any data related to abortion, we do not know how many of these children would have been killed prior to birth through abortion,” she said. “But very likely many died before abortion limitations but their deaths were not counted.” “These are children whose abnormalities are significant enough that they would have died at some point,” she said, “but rather than killing them before birth, they’re being born and then dying after birth, when they begin to be counted in our statistics.” As for the purported rise in total infant mortality, [PERSON] noted that other causes of infant mortality “include deaths from complications of prematurity, sudden infant death syndrome, accidents, or other events.” “The most recent study did not delineate between pro-life and pro-choice states, so we don’t know if deaths are increased in pro-life states, but if that association is confirmed, we need to seriously examine possible contributing factors unique to these states,” she said. Such factors “may include increased poverty, family breakdown, maternity care deserts, or lack of health care access. Merely blaming abortion limitations is dishonest and avoids directing attention to the real causes.” Some researchers have further argued that total abortions have actually increased in the wake of Roe’s repeal despite the large number of states that have enacted partial or near-total bans on the procedure. Skop cautioned that pro-life advocates should be “skeptical” of such claims. She argued that much of the research showing increases in abortion relies on what are effectively estimates, such as tracking the number of abortion pills dispensed without actually confirming that the mothers took the pills. “A woman could order [the drugs] online and then change her mind, or could request them just to have them on hand if she should become pregnant,” she said. “There’s no evidence these abortions are occurring; rather it’s just that these are drugs being distributed.” It’s “probably more helpful to look at what’s happening with our birth rate,” she argued. “And I think that it’s been demonstrated, in pro-life states, that our birth rate has increased slightly.” Some fertility data have indeed indicated that births have risen in some places with abortion bans. “So that tells me that abortions are being avoided, that women are choosing to bring their babies to birth,” Skop said. “And that’s a good thing,” she added. “In my practice, women may consider an abortion, but if they choose to continue the pregnancy, they inevitably are happy that they did.” “Most initially undesired pregnancies become very much wanted babies,” she said. As with many other aspects of their war against [LOCATION], Ukrainians have reacted to the outcome of the [LOCATION] presidential election with a certain dark humor. [TIME] after the election, [LOCATION] social media was full of jokes, including by soldiers commenting that they are “preparing to go home soon, since the war will end in [TIME].” They were referring, of course, to President-elect [PERSON] long-standing claim that he could stop the war in a day if he were elected. [LOCATION] has many reasons to be concerned about a second [ORGANIZATION] presidency. [PERSON] has not said how he would end the war, or even under what conditions. In his debate with Vice President [PERSON], in [DATE], he refused to say that he wanted [LOCATION] to win. He has also repeatedly complained about the amount of military assistance that [LOCATION] has been giving [PERSON]. In the background, there is his longtime admiration for Russian President [PERSON], and [ORGANIZATION]’s running mate, [PERSON], who was one of the first Republicans to embrace indifference to [LOCATION] as a policy position: “I don’t really care what happens to [LOCATION] one [STREET] or the other,” he said in [DATE]. And in polling before the election, where a clear majority of Democrats agreed that [LOCATION] had a responsibility to support [LOCATION], only about a third of Republican voters said that it did. All this has led many to fear that [LOCATION]—by far [ORGANIZATION]’s biggest arms supplier—might cut off the flow of aid, or even allow [LOCATION] to dictate the terms of peace. But the reality of the war has made Ukrainians pragmatic: the situation can always get worse, but they still need to adjust and search for a [STREET] out to survive. Setting aside [ORGANIZATION]’s campaign rhetoric, Ukrainian President [PERSON] is preparing to work with him. After all, Ukrainians lived through the first [ORGANIZATION] administration and have some sense of what they are getting: dealmaking and attempts to flatter [PERSON], but also, eventually, a major sale of lethal arms, including Javelin antitank weapons, which have been critical in the fight against [LOCATION]. [PERSON]’s task is and will remain to find ways to receive what his government needs to defend the population in the long run. For [LOCATION] , then, the meaning of a second [ORGANIZATION] administration is complicated. Even if the initial phase of [ORGANIZATION]’s return to power is full of speculations, leaks, and disappointments—and even if [LOCATION] decides to slow or freeze military aid, causing even more casualties and losses of territory—Kyiv knows that [LOCATION] is unlikely to simply cede victory to [PERSON]. It is indisputable that [ORGANIZATION] dislikes long and expensive foreign wars. And Ukrainians themselves are ready to end the war—but from a position of strength. READING THE CROWD Throughout the war, [PERSON] has never taken American support for granted. In sheer magnitude, [LOCATION] has provided more military assistance than any other country, and in some crucial areas, such as cyberwarfare, advanced air defense systems, and intelligence, [LOCATION] resources cannot be substituted. Yet even [DATE], [LOCATION] began planning for a future of waning [LOCATION] support. Following the unsuccessful counteroffensive in [DATE], [LOCATION] officials interpreted the increasingly negative assessments of the war in the [LOCATION] media as a sign that [LOCATION]’s military assistance might shrink. To prepare for this, the [PERSON] government accelerated efforts to expand domestic weapons production and strengthened relations with other partners in [LOCATION], as well as with [LOCATION] and [LOCATION]. Kyiv also began stepping up its efforts to sell the international community on its so-called peace formula—[LOCATION]’s multilateral initiative, first announced in [DATE], that aims at recruiting a large group of countries around key issues that will need to be addressed at the end of the war, including food security and environmental damage, as well as the restoration of energy infrastructure and nuclear safety. (So far, some 90 countries have endorsed the formula.) Ukrainian sappers building defenses along the frontline, near [LOCATION], [LOCATION], [DATE] [ORGANIZATION] of the 24th [ORGANIZATION] Separate Mechanized Brigade of [ORGANIZATION] officials have also tried to ensure that if they are forced to negotiate with [LOCATION] , they will not be alone and that the Ukrainian vision of peace will already be on the table. [LOCATION] has made clear, for example, that humanitarian issues such as the return of Ukrainian children taken to [LOCATION] and the exchange of prisoners of war could become the basis for future negotiations. But whatever the future of [LOCATION] aid, [PERSON] has long recognized the need to retain the support of both major parties in [LOCATION] . That lesson was learned during [ORGANIZATION]’s first impeachment trial in [DATE], when [ORGANIZATION]’s phone call to [PERSON], asking the Ukrainian president to investigate [PERSON], became a primary focus of the inquiry. For [DATE], the first [PERSON] cabinet had worked with [PERSON]. At the time of the impeachment, [PERSON] was still in [ORGANIZATION], but Ukrainians understood that they needed to engage with Democrats. Conversely, after [LOCATION]’s full-scale invasion in [DATE], despite the fact that the Democrats were now in power and were their primary interlocutors, [PERSON] continued to reach out to Republicans, as well. That understanding of [LOCATION] politics has been particularly important in obtaining continued military assistance; none of the five [LOCATION] aid bills could have been passed without Republican votes in [ORGANIZATION]. In [DATE], as the Republican-controlled [ORGANIZATION] held up a further aid bill, [PERSON] began reaching out to even more legislators and others from the Republican camp. In [DATE], [PERSON] welcomed [ORGANIZATION] CEO [PERSON] for a meeting in [LOCATION]. And [LOCATION] pursued these contacts until the long-delayed aid package was finally approved by [ORGANIZATION] in [DATE]. In the end, Republican Speaker of the [ORGANIZATION] [PERSON], who had been a skeptic of more [LOCATION] support, was fully persuaded: “I think providing aid to [LOCATION] right now is critically important,” he said, in announcing his endorsement of the bill. Kyiv’s courtship continued throughout the presidential campaign. In [DATE], following [ORGANIZATION], [PERSON] had his first call with [PERSON] since he left [ORGANIZATION], in [DATE]. (At the time, [PERSON] called it a “very good phone call.”) [DATE], [PERSON] also visited [LOCATION] for a [ORGANIZATION] meeting, where he engaged with a large group of Republican politicians. Then, in [DATE], [PERSON] received Senator [PERSON], a [ORGANIZATION] ally, and other members of [ORGANIZATION] in Kyiv. After the meeting, [PERSON] called for delivering more weapons to [PERSON], noting that Ukrainians are “trying to stop the Russians so we don’t have to fight them.” [PERSON] welcoming [LOCATION] Senator [PERSON] in [LOCATION], [DATE] [ORGANIZATION] These efforts culminated in [DATE], when [PERSON] again visited [LOCATION] and met with both [PERSON] and Vice President [PERSON] . As some analysts have noted, [ORGANIZATION]’s willingness to meet with [PERSON] during [DATE] of his campaign was not a given, and the fact that he did so shows that he was taking [LOCATION] seriously. By this point, [PERSON] had an additional priority: with the war situation becoming increasingly tough and some Western allies beginning to show signs of war fatigue, [LOCATION] wanted to show that it had a viable strategy for winning. Thus, [PERSON] took the opportunity to present his “victory plan” not just to the [PERSON] administration but to both presidential candidates, as well. Although its most important parts remain confidential, the victory plan outlined, among other things, how [LOCATION] would use more sophisticated kinds of weapons to change the reality on the battlefield: by waging a more high-tech war, [LOCATION] would be able to destroy [LOCATION]’s logistics hubs, thereby preventing [LOCATION]’s control of airspace along the front and decreasing pressure on [LOCATION]’s infantry. So far, the [LOCATION] reaction to the [PERSON] plan—whether from the [PERSON] administration or [ORGANIZATION]’s team—has been hard to assess, but for Kyiv it was another [STREET] to make clear that it could work with whoever captured [ORGANIZATION]. LEARNING FROM [ORGANIZATION] After [DATE] and [DATE] of fighting, Ukrainians hold few illusions about the limits of [LOCATION] backing. They have long since recognized that the [LOCATION] strategy—massive amounts of military assistance, but with many constraints on kinds of weapons and how they can be used—has allowed them to sustain the fight but fallen short of letting them change the direction of the war. At the same time, they are not engaging in wishful thinking or expecting radical breakthroughs with [ORGANIZATION]. Of course, what is said by a head of state must be taken seriously. When [PERSON] repeats that he is planning to destroy the Ukrainian state, it is naive for Ukrainians to think he doesn’t mean it. With [PERSON], however, it is unclear what he really means when he vows to end the war in [TIME]. For one thing, it does not appear that he has much leverage with [LOCATION], and there is also little indication that [LOCATION] is prepared to listen—unless [ORGANIZATION] agrees to allow [LOCATION] to occupy the rest of [LOCATION], which seems highly unlikely. But Ukrainians have something else to go on: how [PERSON] dealt with [LOCATION] and [LOCATION] during his previous term in [ORGANIZATION]. Consider the recollections of former [LOCATION] Ambassador to [LOCATION] Marie Yovanovitch. In a meeting with the American [LOCATION] community in [LOCATION] [DATE] before the [DATE] election, Yovanovitch described [PERSON]’s press conference in [DATE] when he said that he would trust the Russian president more than his own intelligence community. According to [PERSON], [PERSON] also refused to push back on [LOCATION] over its attack on a [LOCATION] ship in international waters in [LOCATION]; later, he also canceled joint U.S.-Ukrainian naval exercises. (In [DATE], [PERSON] herself was recalled from her post by [PERSON].) In [DATE], the [ORGANIZATION] campaign was hardly more reassuring. At [ORGANIZATION] and [PERSON] campaign rallies that I attended in [LOCATION] and [LOCATION] in [DATE], neither mentioned the war in [LOCATION], but their recurring promises to stop “financing foreign wars” was loudly cheered by the audience. Nonetheless, [PERSON] supporters themselves show a range of views about [LOCATION], and even include a sizable number of Ukrainian Americans. In those two swing states, Ukrainian Americans supporting [PERSON] were terrified by the possibility that [LOCATION] might end support for [LOCATION]. But many others I spoke with supported [PERSON]. Father [PERSON] of [ORGANIZATION] in [LOCATION], who offered a benediction at [ORGANIZATION] rally in [ORGANIZATION] before the assassination attempt, is a vocal supporter of the former president. Many echo the arguments that [PERSON] himself makes: the war didn’t start under [PERSON], and it was [PERSON] who provided [LOCATION] with its first lethal weapon—the [PERSON]. A [LOCATION] soldier unpacking U.S.-supplied Javelin antitank missiles, near [LOCATION], [DATE] [ORGANIZATION] in Kyiv hope that [PERSON] and his team will become more pragmatic once they start getting security briefings. During [ORGANIZATION]’s first term, there was no visible breakthrough, but the level of [LOCATION] support for [LOCATION] did grow little by little, mainly because over time there was a better understanding of the situation on the ground. That could apply again: once [PERSON] is confronted with what [LOCATION] is doing on the battlefield, how deeply [LOCATION] and [LOCATION] (a hated enemy of [ORGANIZATION]) are involved, and how effective [LOCATION] can be at destroying Russian weapons, he may see that it is crucial for [LOCATION] to do everything possible to prevent a Russian victory. But in a larger [STREET], [LOCATION] also understands that [ORGANIZATION]’s ultimate policy direction will depend on which people become most prominent in his administration. [ORGANIZATION]’s announcement on [DATE] that the Republican congressman and retired [PERSON] would be his national security adviser sets down one marker. In [LOCATION], [PERSON] has been called a [LOCATION] skeptic, and he is known for questioning [LOCATION] aid packages to [LOCATION] and claiming that [LOCATION] should share more of the burden. He has also said, in the run-up to the election, that there should be some kind of “diplomatic resolution” to end the war. But [PERSON]’s precise views may be more complex. During the early stages of the war, [PERSON] was engaged with Ukrainian civil society members and was adamant in his criticism of [LOCATION]. He also said that [PERSON] was not doing enough to support [LOCATION], even arguing, in [DATE], that [LOCATION] should send military advisers into [LOCATION]. “Let’s win this damn war!” he said at the time. More recently, he has said that if [LOCATION] did not want to negotiate, [ORGANIZATION] might try “taking the handcuffs off of long-range weapons we provided [LOCATION],” thus allowing [LOCATION] to raise the cost to [LOCATION]. Also important may be [PERSON], who in [LOCATION] remains an ambivalent figure. On the one hand, his [ORGANIZATION] satellite network has been crucial to [LOCATION]’s war effort. But in [DATE] [DATE], he denied a Ukrainian request to use [ORGANIZATION] over [ORGANIZATION], at a time when Ukrainians were targeting Russian warships in the area with no remorse. Musk claimed that he wanted to prevent a scenario in which [PERSON] might use a nuclear weapon. Musk’s move hindered Ukrainian operations, but Ukrainian forces nonetheless managed to make successful strikes on Russian targets in [LOCATION]. At first, the Ukrainian government held back criticism of [DATE], but [PERSON] challenged the tech billionaire later that fall, after [PERSON] outlined his own version of a “peace plan” in which he seemed to echo [LOCATION]’s own narratives about the war and suggested that [LOCATION] should be allowed to keep [ORGANIZATION]. According to an [DATE] report in [ORGANIZATION] , it was also in [DATE] that Musk began to have occasional contacts with [PERSON]. ([LOCATION] has denied any contacts beyond a single phone call in which they discussed “space as well as current and future technologies.”) Still, Musk briefly joined [ORGANIZATION]’s call with [PERSON] after the election, and, according to reports, told the Ukrainian president that he would keep sending [ORGANIZATION] ground stations to [LOCATION]. HARD JUST GOT HARDER There have been many attempts to decipher what [ORGANIZATION] means when he talks about ending the war in [TIME]. Apparently, he would persuade [PERSON] to negotiate, although it is unclear how he would do this. (It is possible that Musk, who brags about talking to [PERSON] directly, or Hungarian Prime Minister [PERSON], who is friendly with both [PERSON] and [PERSON], could be potential brokers of such talks.) Even if such a channel were opened, however, it is far from clear what, if anything, it might yield. Many Ukrainians view the prospect of [PERSON] talks in the light of [ORGANIZATION]’s attempts during his first term to deal with North Korean leader [PERSON]. In the end, the special rapport that the former president cultivated didn’t lead to any substantial agreement. And [PERSON], over whom [LOCATION] has even more limited leverage, is a stronger leader than [PERSON]. Already, in the immediate aftermath of the election, leading Russian propagandists have asserted that [LOCATION] doesn’t care about any peace initiatives and warned [LOCATION] not to issue ultimatums. They also reiterated that [PERSON] intends to destroy [LOCATION]. In the end, there is no reason to have the [LOCATION] president be the broker of peace if that role is reduced to pressuring [PERSON] to submit to [LOCATION]’s conditions. [PERSON] and [PERSON] at [LOCATION], [LOCATION], [DATE] [ORGANIZATION] In [DATE], I talked to a group of Ukrainian soldiers close to the Russian border. They freely admitted how tired they were of the war, but they also were unanimous in opposing negotiations with [PERSON]. As they saw it, the [ORGANIZATION] would use a cease-fire to arm itself, strengthen [LOCATION]’s war economy, and prepare for an even more devastating invasion of towns such as [ORGANIZATION], Kharkiv, and [ORGANIZATION] in the near future. And if that happened, Russian retaliation against the families of Ukrainian soldiers would be extreme. This has already been shown in Russian-occupied territories, where Russian forces have targeted anyone who served in [ORGANIZATION] before 2022. By now, almost every [LOCATION] has a family member engaged in the war effort, so every [LOCATION] would be a target. To deal with an uncertain American future, [LOCATION]’s strategy is straightforward: to explain that a Russian victory would be extremely dangerous for [LOCATION]. Not only would it strengthen [LOCATION], [LOCATION], and [LOCATION]; it would also tempt other autocracies to invade their own neighbors. At the same time, [PERSON] can remind [LOCATION] that a very large portion of the military aid that [LOCATION] has provided to [LOCATION] is largely spent at home: the American defense industry receives government funds to produce ammunition on American soil by American workers. From afar, the [PERSON] government’s rush to embrace the incoming administration may look like sheer opportunism. But [PERSON] is also being strategic. It knows that the [PERSON] administration will have little window for action in the time it has left and that [LOCATION] must quickly prepare for a different world. What the [PERSON] administration has presented to the press as a final financial package—$6 billion in additional security assistance—was planned a while ago. (In fact, it is simply the remaining part of the $61 billion aid package passed in [DATE].) In [DATE] before the election, [PERSON] tried to persuade [PERSON] to support a formal [ORGANIZATION] invitation for [LOCATION], arguing that it could form a part of his foreign policy legacy. After [ORGANIZATION]’s election victory, it is hard to imagine that [PERSON] will try anything so significant. And under [PERSON], joining [ORGANIZATION] will likely be off the table. Yet the fact is that throughout all the hardest moments of [LOCATION]’s history, [LOCATION] has stood up for the country and its people, making it possible for the nation to survive. Thus far, this has been true under both Republican and Democratic presidents, even when they have differed significantly on policy. It is also true that prolonged war is not something Ukrainians like. Instead of supporting the country “as long as it takes,” as [PERSON] has often said, they would prefer more decisive measures. Whatever happens after [DATE], it will be critical for [LOCATION] to get further funds and weapons in [DATE]. If [PERSON] does try to talk to [LOCATION], [LOCATION] will need to be in the strongest position possible on the battlefield. Ukrainians know that it won’t be easy to ensure [LOCATION]’s continued support. But nothing has been easy up to this point, either. Loading... [PERSON], an economist at [ORGANIZATION], estimated that [LOCATION] has between 35,000 and 40,000 undocumented workers, primarily in food processing and construction. A memo from [ORGANIZATION] [DATE] laid out the mechanics of a large-scale mass deportation effort. Deporting immigrants who lack legal status on the scale [ORGANIZATION] envisions would mean arresting millions of individuals; placing them in proceedings before immigration judges; litigating those cases in [STREET], including appeals; and then removing them from [LOCATION]. It was last used to intern Japanese Americans during World War II, for which [ORGANIZATION], presidents and the courts have apologized. “We look back on that with shame and as a tragic mistake. Participants in [ORGANIZATION] Cheyenne’s annual Silent Witness [DATE] carried images and silhouettes representing their loved ones from [ORGANIZATION] Building on [ORGANIZATION] to [ORGANIZATION], where domestic violence survivor [PERSON] shared her experience with abuse. [PERSON] met her abuser when she was in [DATE]. She said he was handsome and made more money than she did. At 26, [PERSON] eloped with him. “It was very small, because he did weddings for a living, so he hated weddings,” [PERSON] told the crowd. “He controlled the whole thing. I mean, looking back, all the signs were there.” Going through a slide show, with pictures and documents from her [DATE] married to her abuser, [PERSON] continued to tell the crowd about how during her second pregnancy, after giving birth to twins and again being pregnant with twins, her husband would hit her, even kicking her pregnant stomach. [PERSON] gave birth [DATE], in [DATE], to twins, a boy and girl. Her son did not survive, and her daughter was only 3 pounds, 9 ounces. “(My abuser’s) wedding band fit over her wrist,” [PERSON] told the crowd. “You don’t know how tiny that is.” “The (operating) room was just deadly quiet,” [PERSON] said. “They pulled (my son) out, and his head was all smashed in. The priest came, and he had holy water in a seashell and gave him (and his sister) last rites.” [PERSON] has two other twin boys, and at one point, one of her sons was hit repeatedly by her abuser, leaving a hand mark on his face. They were living in [LOCATION] at the time, and [ORGANIZATION] was called, and [PERSON] thought someone would finally help. The claim was marked as “unsubstantiated” because [PERSON]’s abuser signed papers telling [ORGANIZATION] that his family didn’t need help. “Are my twins, at [DATE], going to say anything against their dad? … No, they’re not,” [PERSON] said. “When I got kicked in my second trimester in the stomach, and he picked me up on my neck until I passed out? I came to with blood (on me) and my sons standing over me. And when one of them ran to the neighbor’s house, their dad picked them up like a bag of trash and said, ‘We don’t tell anybody about this.’” [PERSON] and her children were abused by her former husband until she was able to leave in [DATE]. [PERSON] is Roman Catholic, and when she was finally able to leave her abuser, her abuse was so well documented with the church that she was able to receive an annulment, which is incredibly rare in Catholicism. [PERSON]’s first marriage wasn’t her only experience with abuse. Her second marriage was abusive, as well. [PERSON] joked that she married a cowboy with a gun because she thought he would protect her; however, she was unaware of his undiagnosed mental health issues. She was able to share her experience as a survivor, but many of those in attendance were there to mourn their loved ones who did not survive their abusers. A large group of family members joined the march to memorialize [PERSON], a [LOCATION] woman who was killed in [DATE]. “She worked in the hospital, she worked as a waitress, she volunteered for Meals on Wheels, she helped the homeless,” [PERSON]’s mother, [LOCATION], told the crowd. “... We are very proud of our daughter.” [LOCATION] was supported by her husband and [PERSON]’s father, [LOCATION], as she briefly spoke with the group about her daughter. [PERSON] also shared the story of her daughter, [PERSON], who was killed and found in the basement of [ORGANIZATION] in south [PERSON]. At the time of [ORGANIZATION] death, she left behind a 2½-year-old boy; the man that killed [PERSON] was not her son’s father. [PERSON] originally didn’t want him to call her mom, because she didn’t want to erase her daughter, she told the crowd. It wasn’t until [DATE], when she and her grandson talked about it that she felt OK being called Mom. “He told me, ‘I got a mom up in heaven, and I got a mom right here,’” [PERSON] told the crowd. According to [ORGANIZATION], 33.9% of women and 30.5% of men in the state experience intimate partner physical violence, intimate partner sexual violence and/or intimate partner stalking in their lifetimes. According to [PERSON], it’s important to share these stories to support each other, and help alleviate the guilt and shame that abuse can cause. “A young woman came up to me, and she lost her cousin, and she said, ‘You know, I heard that you know, I heard you still carry the shame that you picked a bad one,’” [PERSON] told [ORGANIZATION]. “She said, ‘It’s not your shame to carry you didn’t pick a bad one. He picked a good one.’” For [PERSON], hearing that it wasn’t her fault from another woman who had lost someone to abuse was freeing. “He sought me out because I was good, and there was something so freeing about that,” [PERSON] said. “Because this entire time I thought there was something so fundamentally wrong with me for my choices and how it impacted my children. I’ve never thought that he saw something in me that he could manipulate and control and coerce, and eventually abuse and try to destroy, until I left in the middle of the night with my three children.” Telling stories like these is about breaking cycles of abuse, [PERSON] said. A display of the victims’ silhouettes and a brief account of their death were set up at the library, and will remain there for the rest of [DATE], according to a news release. This display will be available for public viewing, along with proclamations from [LOCATION] Gov. [PERSON] and [PERSON] Mayor [PERSON] about ending violence against women. The display includes the stories of [PERSON], [PERSON], [LOCATION], [PERSON], [PERSON], [PERSON], [PERSON], [PERSON], [PERSON], and a silhouette honoring the missing and murdered indigenous women of [LOCATION]. The march and the presentation on [ORGANIZATION] are some of the activities hosted by [ORGANIZATION] during [DATE] of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, which runs from [DATE] through [DATE], according to the news release. The initiative was started by [ORGANIZATION] at [ORGANIZATION] in [DATE], and is recognized by activists around the world as a time to raise awareness in their communities and to call for the elimination of all types of gender-based violence, according to the release.
